newsitem.title: UK: UBS analysts see upside risk for wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: UBS analysts see upside risk for wheat prices.

text.p: Wheat prices are likely to stay volatile in 1997 on tight stocks and with a prospect they will firm later in the year, UBS Ltd reseachers say in their latest Commodities Outlook.
They also find that fundamentals don't explain the present high price for coffee and add that prospects for global economic expansion remain the wild card for the base metals.
"Visions of increasing base metal output cloud price prospects but similar hallucinations failed to materialise last year," says the UBS report.
It says aluminium demand should exceed even a 3.0 percent growth in supply in 1997 but copper demand may lag the expansion of supply.
The wheat market is seen volatile "as stocks-to-use ratios are still tight and major uncertainties cloud the world market".

These include open questions on EU subsidies, the US export enhancement programme and northern hemisphere crops but UBS thinks that "chances are more upside than downside and prices should firm later in 1997".
It sees a general unease in the coffee market because fundamentals do not explain current strength.
"Development of coffee prices will primarily depend on this year's harvest in Brazil - here crop estimates still vary substantially," says the report .
Chicago wheat futures are around $3.75 per bushel at present after being above $5 for much of 1996 and spiking to a record at $7.50 a year ago.
Coffee futures rallied this year by almost 50 percent whilst base metals showed modest gains. - - London Newsroom +171 44 542 7729
